topic_ko: Frederick Law Olmsted — 미국 조경 건축의 아버지
_note: 인물 일대기(실용문). 주제/주장/빈칸/함축 등 학술형은 제외하고 내용일치·어법·어휘·순서·삽입·요약·서술형만 작성.

passage: Frederick Law Olmsted, remembered today as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822.
In his boyhood he frequently traveled through the countryside with his father, a man devoted to fine scenery.
At fourteen he was getting ready to enroll at Yale College.
A severe case of sumac poisoning ruined his eyesight, however, and he was never able to enter the school.
Rather than going to college, he learned about the world by working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
In 1858 he and Calvert Vaux won the competition to design New York City's Central Park with their "Greensward Plan."
Throughout the Civil War he acted as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission.
After his death in 1903 his sons carried on his ideas, and in 1979 his Brookline home and office became a National Historic Site.
theme.question: Frederick Law Olmsted에 관한 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: 소년 시절 아버지와 함께 시골을 자주 여행했다.
심한 옻나무 중독으로 시력이 상해 Yale College에 들어가지 못했다.
대학 대신 점원, 선원, 농부로 일하며 세상을 배웠다.
1858년 Calvert Vaux와 함께 Central Park 설계 공모전에서 당선되었다.
남북 전쟁이 끝난 뒤에야 미국 위생위원회 사무총장이 되었다.
theme.explanation_ko: 본문 [7]은 그가 남북 전쟁 '내내(Throughout the Civil War)' 위생위원회 사무총장으로 활동했다고 밝힌다. 전쟁이 끝난 뒤에야 그 직책을 맡았다는 ⑤는 본문과 일치하지 않는다.
theme.distractor_ko: ①시골 여행, ②옻나무 중독으로 인한 진학 좌절, ③점원·선원·농부 경력, ④1858년 공모전 당선은 모두 본문과 일치한다.

passage: Frederick Law Olmsted, known as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822.
As a boy he often traveled to the countryside with his father, who loved scenery.
At fourteen he was preparing himself to study at Yale College.
But he could not enter because of a severe sumac poisoning that damaging his eyesight.
Instead of attending a college, he gained experience working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
In 1858 he worked with Calvert Vaux and won the design competition for Central Park.
During the Civil War he served as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission.
In 1979 the National Park Service designated his Brookline home and office as a National Historic Site.
grammar.explanation_ko: ③ 관계대명사 that이 이끄는 절에는 정동사가 필요하므로 분사 damaging이 아니라 과거시제 damaged가 되어야 한다. ③이 정답.
grammar.distractor_ko: ①주어를 보충하는 과거분사 known, ②사람 선행사를 받는 계속적 용법 who, ④전치사 of 뒤의 동명사 attending, ⑤문장의 본동사 designated는 모두 옳다.

passage: Frederick Law Olmsted, known as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822.
As a boy he often traveled to the countryside with his father, who loved scenery.
At fourteen he was preparing to study at Yale College, but a severe sumac poisoning damaged his eyesight.
Instead of attending a college, he gained experience working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
In 1858 he worked with Calvert Vaux and lost the design competition for New York City's Central Park.
During the Civil War he served as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission.
Although he passed away in 1903, his sons and successors continued his design philosophy.
In 1979 the National Park Service designated his Brookline home and office as a National Historic Site.
vocab.explanation_ko: ③ Olmsted는 "Greensward Plan"으로 Central Park 설계 공모전에서 '당선되었다'. 그것이 그의 대표 업적이므로 lost(패배했다)는 문맥과 정반대이며 won이 적절하다.
vocab.distractor_ko: ①severe(심한) 중독, ②gained(쌓았다) 경험, ④successors(후계자), ⑤designated(지정했다)는 모두 문맥에 맞는다.

order.given: Frederick Law Olmsted, known as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822. As a boy he often traveled to the countryside with his father, who loved scenery.

blocks.A: During the Civil War he then took on public duty, serving as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission until the fighting ended.
blocks.B: At fourteen he prepared to enter Yale College, but a severe sumac poisoning damaged his eyesight, so he worked instead as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
blocks.C: That practical training paid off in 1858, when he and Calvert Vaux won the competition to design New York City's Central Park.

order.explanation_ko: 유년기 다음으로 (B)14세의 진학 좌절과 현장 경력, (C)그 경험이 1858년 공모전 당선으로 이어짐, (A)그 후 남북 전쟁 중 공직 수행의 시간 순서가 자연스럽다. (B)-(C)-(A).
order.distractor_ko: (C)의 'That practical training(그 실무 경험)'은 (B)에서 언급된 점원·선원·농부 경력을 받으므로 (C)가 (B)보다 앞설 수 없다.

insert.insert_sentence: Instead of attending a college, he gained experience working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.

passage_marked.text: Frederick Law Olmsted, known as the father of American landscape architecture, was born in 1822.
As a boy he often traveled to the countryside with his father, who loved scenery.
At fourteen he was preparing to study at Yale College, but a severe sumac poisoning damaged his eyesight and kept him out.
In 1858 that practical background helped him and Calvert Vaux win the design competition for New York City's Central Park.
During the Civil War he served as General Secretary of the United States Sanitary Commission.

insert.explanation_ko: 주어진 문장의 'Instead of attending a college(대학에 다니는 대신)'는 ③ 앞 문장의 진학 좌절을 받고, ④의 'that practical background(그 실무 경력)'가 가리키는 대상을 제공하므로 ③ 자리에 들어간다.
insert.distractor_ko: 주어진 문장이 없으면 ④의 'that practical background'가 무엇을 가리키는지 알 수 없게 된다.

passage: Frederick Law Olmsted was born in 1822 and grew up traveling the countryside with a father who loved scenery.
At fourteen he prepared for Yale College.
A severe sumac poisoning damaged his eyesight and kept him from entering.
He therefore worked as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer instead.
In 1858 he and Calvert Vaux won the Central Park design competition.
He served the United States Sanitary Commission during the Civil War.
His sons carried on his design philosophy after his death in 1903.
In 1979 his Brookline home and office were named a National Historic Site.
summary.summary_template: Although illness __(A)__ Olmsted from entering college, the varied work he took up instead prepared him for a career whose __(B)__ was later honored with a National Historic Site.
summary.explanation_ko: 옻나무 중독이라는 병이 대학 진학을 (A)막았고(prevented), 그 대신 쌓은 다양한 경력이 이끈 그의 (B)유산(legacy)이 국가 사적지 지정으로 기려졌다. ⑤가 정답.
summary.distractor_ko: (A)는 encouraged/released가 아니라 prevented, (B)는 failure/wealth가 아니라 legacy여야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 우리말과 같은 뜻이 되도록 <보기>의 단어를 모두 배열하여 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 대학에 다니는 대신, 그는 점원, 선원, 농부로 일하면서 경험을 쌓았다.
writing.answer: Instead of attending a college, he gained experience working as a clerk, a sailor, and a farmer.
writing.explanation_ko: 전치사구 Instead of + 동명사(attending) + 주절 he gained experience + 동시 상황 분사구문 working as ~.

writing.question: 다음 우리말을 <조건>에 맞게 영작하시오.
writing.ko_prompt: 그는 1903년에 세상을 떠났지만, 그의 아들들과 후계자들이 그의 설계 철학을 이어 갔다.
conditions: 양보의 접속사 Although 로 시작할 것
passed away 와 design philosophy 를 모두 포함할 것
writing.answer: Although he passed away in 1903, his sons and successors continued his design philosophy.
writing.explanation_ko: Although + 절(양보) + 주절. pass away(세상을 떠나다), design philosophy(설계 철학).

writing.question: 다음 밑줄 친 문장을 우리말로 해석하시오.
writing.en_prompt: At age 14, he was preparing himself to study at Yale College, but he could not enter due to a severe sumac poisoning that damaged his eyesight.
writing.answer: 14세에 그는 Yale College에서 공부할 준비를 하고 있었지만, 그의 시력을 손상시킨 심한 옻나무 중독 때문에 입학할 수 없었다.
writing.explanation_ko: due to + 명사구(~ 때문에), that damaged his eyesight는 poisoning을 수식하는 관계절. '준비했다'와 '입학하지 못했다'를 구분해 해석해야 한다.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 흐름상 빈칸에 들어갈 한 단어를 본문에서 찾아 쓰시오.
writing.context: In 1858, he worked with Calvert Vaux and won the design ___________ for New York City's Central Park with the "Greensward Plan."
writing.explanation_ko: 본문에서 그는 Central Park 설계 'competition(공모전)'에서 당선되었다.

writing.question: 다음 글을 읽고, 요약문의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 단어를 본문에 근거하여 쓰시오.
writing.summary: A severe sumac poisoning damaged Olmsted's (A)___________, so he never entered Yale; decades later the National Park Service honored his (B)___________ with a National Historic Site.
writing.explanation_ko: (A) 옻나무 중독이 손상시킨 것은 시력(eyesight)이며, (B) 국립공원관리청이 기린 것은 그의 유산(legacy)이다.
